title: Philadelphia's Academy Museum Closes Despite Offer of Temporary Funding
summary:
The Academy of Natural Sciences museum in Philadelphia closed on September 30. The Academy was founded in 1812 and opened to the public in 1828. In 1868, it became the first place in the world to display a dinosaur skeleton.

For generations, visiting the museum has been a family tradition. When the closure was announced on September 1, thousands of families came for a final visit. Alexandria McCormick visited with her husband and six children. She said her childhood visits inspired her love of natural history, and she was sad that her children might not have similar experiences.

Drexel University took over financial responsibility for the Academy in 2011. Drexel said costs rose and attendance declined after the pandemic. During the museum's final weeks, however, attendance increased sharply and revenue was more than 20 times higher than last September.

Some supporters criticized Drexel for giving only one month's notice and for not explaining how much it would cost to keep the museum open. Drexel said it remained deeply committed to protecting the Academy's legacy.

The Academy holds more than 19 million scientific specimens. These are samples kept for study, including Thomas Jefferson's fossil collection and plant samples gathered by Lewis and Clark. The collection also includes 73,000 holotype specimens: preserved samples scientists use as references for defining and naming species. Drexel said it would preserve access for students and researchers, but access for the general public remains unclear.

Less than a week before the closing date, the William Penn Foundation offered one year of bridge funding. Bridge funding is temporary financial support that provides time to explore a lasting solution. Drexel said it was exploring possible work with the foundation but needed a plan for long-term sustainability before considering reopening.

Philadelphia's city council proposed zoning changes to make selling the museum building or converting it to other uses more difficult. It also plans public hearings to investigate how the closure happened and consider possible solutions. Whether the museum will reopen remains uncertain.
why_it_matters: The museum has provided families with opportunities to learn about natural history and holds specimens used for scientific study. Its closure raises questions about public access and how it could operate in the future.
